title: Peregrine retail integration — raw worklog
content:
Call log 2026-02-12 (raw)
Participants: Peregrine (CTO - Laura M., Head of Platform - Ben R., Lead SRE - Mateo), Redwood: Ava (SE), Samir (runtime), Rhea (security)

High-level ask
- Peregrine wants a private deployment in their GCP VPC (multi-project) for chat+search assistant across 2 EU regions.
- Hard requirements: EU data residency, HIPAA adjacency (they handle minimal PHI in support cases), p95 latency <= 250ms for short (<=128 tokens) responses, and predictable monthly billing model.
- Starting load: prototyping with 15 qps sustained, occasional peaks to 40 qps for 10-15 minutes. Long-term target 100 qps with reserved capacity.

Notes from discussion
- Network: traffic must go through their egress proxy + internal NGFW. They have strict CIDR allowlist and require mutual TLS between inference nodes and their control plane.
- Identity/KMS: they will use Cloud KMS + HSM-backed keys for model signing and secrets.
- Audit: logs must be forwarded to their Splunk instance with 30d retention for infra events and 365d for access logs.
- Model catalog: they prefer an open model (LlamaX-style) but want Redwood's verified quantized variant for cost. They asked if we can run 8-bit quantized weights on H100/NVIDIA A100 mix — runtime comment: Samir said we support int8/4-fp combos but need a model repro quantization job; quality trade-offs need an eval.
- Privacy: customers’ PII fields will be redacted at the application layer, but Peregrine wants a second layer of metadata stripping at the proxy to be safe. Rhea: suggest using Redwood request filters + a short regex set, but add a note that this is not a guaranteed de-identification.

Gotchas / risks flagged in-call
- CIDR + proxy termination: their network team expects long test cycles. If the private control plane cannot reach their proxy for health checks, we may have to flip to a sidecar health-checker. Ask: can they open port 443 from our control plane IPs?
- Latency SLO vs autoscaling: p95 <=250ms with bursts to 40 qps implies very aggressive autoscaling or pre-warmed reserved capacity. For the pilot, recommend a small dedicated pool with burst buffer.
- KV cache and session affinity: their assistant is chatty and will rely on 3–6k token histories. Continuous batching hurts p95; need to test prefix caching for common assistant footprints. Samir: add a short perf run template.
- Quantization quality regressions: require prompt-based eval harness tied to Canary deploys. They insisted on being able to pin to model revision and to auto-fallback to a higher-precision variant on regressions.

Short-term technical actions (who/when)
- Create minimal perf template for 128-token p95 & 512-token p95 runs (Samir) — target: 2026-02-16.
- Network checklist for Peregrine infra (Ava) — list of IPs, mTLS cert requirements, expected health-check endpoints — target: 2026-02-14.
- Draft data-handling guidance (Rhea) — include recommended request filters, sample redaction rules, and notes on auditability — target: 2026-02-15.
- Provision a test cluster in our private sandbox that mirrors their EU VPC egress behavior (Jonah) — target: 2026-02-20.

Operational notes for onboarding
- Preferred deployment model: Redwood Private (control plane in our SaaS, inference plane in their VPC) — they asked about full air-gapped on-prem later.
- Billing ask: prefer a fixed monthly committed capacity + overage per-token for the first 6 months. Flagging to finance: need a simple quoting template for Dedicated-reserved + 6mo trial.
- Rollouts: propose 3-stage canary (internal QA -> 10% live traffic -> 100%) with automated quality/regression checks and latency guardrails. If quality drops > 2% on the prompt set, auto-fallback and alert.

Perf testing (rough plan)
- Phase 1: baseline with non-quantized model on A100 single-shard to capture p95. Use 128-token & 512-token synth traces that mimic assistant style (short single-turn vs long context).
- Phase 2: test int8 quantized variant, measure relative perplexity on golden prompt set + human-quality check (3 annotators).
- Phase 3: run continuous batching vs no-batching scenarios to measure p95-change. Evaluate prefix cache hit rates on synthetics (target 30–40% hit for repeated prompts).
- Measure costs normalized to token output and report delta to Peregrine in the perf brief.

Open questions to resolve
- Can Peregrine accept our control plane IPs for health checks, or do we need a pull model via their proxy? (Action: Ava)
- Which specific model family do they want evaluated first? They mentioned "RetailAssistant-L" variant — need exact repo/artifact. (Action: Laura to share)
- Legal: what specific language do they require for PHI adjacency? Need to loop legal. (Action: Rhea)
- Does their Splunk team accept JSON lines and gzip? (Action: Ben R.)

Notes to self / internal reminders
- Keep perf template small and reproducible — use k6 + synthetic prompt feeder, export to prometheus -> grafana.
- Add a short FAQ for their network team about mTLS rotation windows; they are sensitive to cert expiry during maintenance.
- Prepare a fallback plan: if quantization fails quality gates, propose using 16-bit mixed precision with slightly larger pool and note cost delta.

Next meeting: 2026-02-19 10:00 CET (follow-up with Peregrine network + security). Goal: confirm network allowlist and agree initial perf test window.

Quick meeting minutes (for email follow-up)
- Agreed: start with private control plane + inference in Peregrine VPC in eu-west1 and eu-west4.
- Action items assigned as above.
- Immediate blockers: confirmation of control plane IPs & model artifact.

End of worklog entry.

-- Ava
(working draft — will convert to a cleaned handoff doc once network answers come in)
